subject: Regulatory data lifecycle: scenarios and options for retention/redaction
messages:
From: Dr. Emily Foster <emily@medsys.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medsys.com
Date: 2027-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on retention and redaction for PHI (MedSys regulatory scenarios)

Hi Lauren / Marissa —

Thanks for taking this. We are evaluating Redwood for a pilot that will ingest patient intake forms and follow-up notes. A couple of regulatory constraints from our side: 1) certain records require a 7-year retention window, 2) in some cases we must be able to irreversibly delete or render personal identifiers unrecoverable on request, and 3) audit trails showing deletion/retention actions need to be exportable for compliance.

Can you confirm:
- For the Private (VPC/on-prem) option, do you support field-level redaction at ingest vs post-ingest redaction?
- Is cryptographic key destruction (to render data unrecoverable) supported as an option for deletion workflows?
- For Hosted API, what are typical retention guarantees and what does deletion actually remove (backups, logs, cached KV state)?
- What evidence can you provide to satisfy our security team (SOC 2, data flow docs, sample audit export)?

Attaching our internal retention policy for reference. We may need a short checklist or scenarios mapping to our requirements so we can present to Legal.

Appreciate a short summary + suggested next steps.

—Emily
Dr. Emily Foster
Head of Data Governance, MedSys Health
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Emily Foster <emily@medsys.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@medsys.com
Date: 2027-04-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on retention and redaction for PHI (MedSys regulatory scenarios)

Hi Emily —

Thanks for the clear background and the policy attachment. High-level answers up front, then a short set of scenario mappings below. I can also set up a technical call with our security lead if you want to walk through a specific workflow.

High level:
- Private (VPC/on-prem): supports both ingest-time and post-ingest redaction. You can run a customer-managed ingest pipeline that tokenizes or masks PII fields before they persist in long-term storage. We also support redaction transforms applied during consumption (search/indexing) if you prefer to keep raw data but redact on read.
- Cryptographic deletion: available when you use envelope encryption with customer-controlled keys (KMS/HSM). Destroying the wrapping key renders stored ciphertext unrecoverable; we document that procedure for customers who require irreversible deletion.
- Hosted API: default hosted retention is configurable per-account; we remove active caches and session KV state on request, but backups may be retained for an account-specific window (we provide timelines and legal process for expedited removal under enterprise contracts). For regulated workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private to give you full control over backups and keying.
- Evidence: we can share a SOC 2 Type II report stub, data flow diagrams, and an exportable audit log format. I'll attach a short Redwood data lifecycle summary.

Scenario mapping (quick):
1) 7-year mandatory retention for a subset of records —> store gold copy in customer-managed storage (Private) with retention TTL set in metadata; audit events show retention policy enforcement.
2) Right-to-erasure for a patient record —> options: a) redact PII fields + retain deidentified record for regulatory reporting, b) cryptographic destruction of encryption key to render record unrecoverable (Private), c) account-level deletion with documented backup purge timeline (Hosted + contract).
3) Audit exports —> per-record audit trails (who/when/policy applied) available; we can provide CSV/JSON export.

Next steps: 1) sign an NDA if helpful, 2) schedule 30-min tech deep dive with Vivek (security/compliance), 3) exchange a short mutual action plan and timeline.

Attaching: redwood-data-lifecycle-summary.pdf (high level).

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Strategic Accounts Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks Emily — and thanks Lauren for the clear mapping. Emily, quick commercial/ops notes so procurement can plan:

Checklist for procurement/legal to review:

- Confirm SLA/retention windows for backups in the selected deployment (we will insert firm timelines in the contract).

- Timeline: do you need pilot data residency within 60 days? 90 days? Please flag critical dates.

If you like, we can draft a short MSA addendum that covers backup purge timelines and key-destruction obligations for regulated records.

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Questions on retention and redaction for PHI (MedSys regulatory scenarios)

Emily — quick technical addendum to the summary Lauren shared. Thanks for the clear requirements. A few concrete notes and limitations so you can present them to your security team: 

1) Cryptographic destruction:
- If you use customer-managed keys (KMIP/KMS/HSM) in Private, destroying the wrapping key is functionally equivalent to irreversible deletion for ciphertext at rest. We will provide a documented key-destruction procedure and notarized confirmation if requested in the scope of an enterprise contract.

2) Field-level redaction vs tokenization:
- Ingest-time redaction (preferred) prevents sensitive fields from ever landing in long-term indexes. Tokenization (retain pointer to token store) lets you keep a deidentified record with a reversible mapping that you control. Both are supported in Private; Hosted supports redaction-by-proxy but reversible token mappings in Hosted are subject to retention/migration rules.

3) Backups and replication windows (Hosted):
- Hosted accounts have snapshot replication for disaster recovery; standard windows are 30 days for incremental snapshots and 90 days archival for certain account tiers. These windows are contract-negotiable for enterprise customers. Deletion requests trigger a staged purge and an audit record; expedited purge can be included in the contract.

4) Auditability:
- We provide exportable audit logs (JSON/CSV) capturing API calls, policy IDs, actor, and timestamp. We also surface per-record policy tags. Logs are retained per your selected retention window and can be pushed to your SIEM via secure forwarding.

Limitations to flag:
- For Hosted, irreversible destruction (in the cryptographic sense) requires customer-managed keying; if you use Redwood-managed keys, destruction is subject to our internal key rotation/retention policies and must be spelled out in contract for any nonstandard behavior.
- Database-level de-duplication and downstream ML cache artifacts: ephemeral caches may persist short-lived derivatives; we can enumerate these and include purge steps in the MSA.

If this looks good I can join the tech call and bring a short runbook that maps their policy clauses to concrete configuration and contract language. Suggest we propose a 30-minute slot next week.

—Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
